paper_sections.title: Promoter haplotypes of interleukin-10 gene linked to cortex plasticity in subjects with risk of Alzheimer's disease
2.8 Statistical analysis involving demographic and neuropsychological data

description.value: The study examined whether interleukin-10 promoter ATA haplotype status is associated with hippocampal functional connectivity and cortical plasticity in amnestic mild cognitive impairment and healthy older adults, and whether connectivity relates to memory performance.

design.value: A cross-sectional 2 × 2 factorial resting-state fMRI study compared subjects with amnestic mild cognitive impairment and healthy controls according to absence or presence of the IL-10 promoter ATA haplotype. Voxel-wise hippocampal functional connectivity was analysed with group-by-haplotype ANOVA, followed by post-hoc group comparisons and correlations with neuropsychological scores.

description.value: Cognitive functioning was evaluated using MMSE.
The degree of dementia was determined using CDR.
AVLT-delayed recall was used to document objective memory performance and was included in the episodic memory composite.
Rey-Osterrieth complex figure test-delayed recall was included in the episodic memory composite.
The digit span test was used to evaluate attention and was included in the non-episodic memory composite.
The symbol digit modalities test was used to evaluate psychomotor speed and was included in the non-episodic memory composite.
Trail-making test-A was used to evaluate attention and psychomotor speed and was included in the non-episodic memory composite.
Trail-making test-B was used to evaluate executive function and was included in the non-episodic memory composite.
The clock-drawing test was used to evaluate visuospatial skills and was included in the non-episodic memory composite.

Composite scores were calculated by converting each test score to a z-score using the means and standard deviations of all subjects, then averaging the z-scores for auditory verbal learning test-delayed recall and Rey-Osterrieth complex figure test-delayed recall.

Composite scores were calculated by converting each test score to a z-score using the means and standard deviations of all subjects, then averaging the z-scores for the digit span test, symbol digit modalities test, trail making test-A, trail making test-B and clock drawing test.

description.value: The first eight volumes were discarded to allow for T1 equilibration effects. The remaining images were corrected for timing differences and motion effects, spatially normalized into the SPM5 Montreal Neurological Institute echo-planar imaging template, resampled to 3 × 3 × 3 mm³ voxels, and smoothed with an 8 × 8 × 8 mm³ Gaussian kernel. REST software was then used to remove the linear trend of time courses and perform temporal bandpass filtering at 0.01–0.08 Hz.

steps.value: The first eight volumes of the scanning session were discarded to allow for T1 equilibration effects.
The remaining images were corrected for timing differences and motion effects.
Participants with head motion of > 3 mm maximum displacement along any axis, or 3° of any type of angular motion were excluded.
The resulting images were spatially normalized into the SPM5 Montreal Neurological Institute echo-planar imaging template using default settings.
The normalized images were smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 8 × 8 × 8 mm³.
REST software was used to remove the linear trend of time courses.

model_settings.value: The bilateral hippocampus was set as the ROI. For each subject, a mean time series for the ROI was computed as the reference time course, and cross-correlation analysis was carried out between the mean signal change in the ROI and the time series of every voxel in the rest of the brain. Six head motion parameters and the mean time series of global, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals were introduced as covariates. Voxelwise-based grey matter volume correction was applied.

estimator.value: cross-correlation analysis followed by Fisher's z-transform
